name: Reconciliation

shots.title: The Space Between
shots.sourceExcerpt:
## EXT. GARDEN BENCH - MORNING

An empty space separates two sisters on a bench. Lea puts a repaired cup in that space.
shots.description: Opening composition: a frontal, static wide shot of a garden bench in morning light. Lea and Sana sit at opposite ends, with a clear empty space between them on the bench. Both face forward. The camera holds, then pushes in very slowly as Lea reaches into the gap and sets down a repaired cup, its mended seams visible. She withdraws her hand. Ending composition: a medium-wide two-shot with the repaired cup alone at the center of the bench between the two sisters.
shots.atmosphere: Quiet, restrained morning stillness with soft natural light and a held distance between the sisters.
shots.music: Silence, or the faintest sustained ambient tone under the garden sounds.

shots.title: It Still Leaks
shots.description: Cut to a static medium close-up of Lea in three-quarter profile from Sana's side of the bench. Sana is a soft out-of-focus shoulder at the frame edge. Lea's eyes stay forward and she does not look at her sister as she speaks. Ending composition: Lea's face, still and averted, holding after the line.
shots.atmosphere: Understated and intimate. The admission is dry and carries quiet weight.

shots.title: Worth Keeping
shots.sourceExcerpt:
### SANA

So do most things worth keeping.
shots.description: Reverse angle to a static medium close-up of Sana in three-quarter profile from Lea's side, matching the opposing eyeline. Lea's shoulder is soft at the frame edge. Sana keeps her gaze forward and does not turn to Lea as she answers. Ending composition: Sana's face holding in the quiet after the line.

dialogue.speaker: SANA
dialogue.text: So do most things worth keeping.

shots.atmosphere: Gentle and tender beneath a reserved surface.
shots.music: A soft, sparse note begins to enter, barely audible.

shots.title: Taking Her Hand
shots.sourceExcerpt: Sana moves the cup aside and takes Lea’s hand. Neither looks at the other. They watch the gardener turn on the sprinklers.
shots.description: Cut to a high-angle close-up of the bench seat. The repaired cup sits in the empty space, with the sisters' hands resting near their own laps. Sana's hand enters, moves the cup aside, then crosses the gap and takes Lea's hand. Ending composition: the two clasped hands filling the space where the cup was, with the cup pushed to the edge of frame.
shots.atmosphere: Small, decisive tenderness. The gap is closed without words.
shots.music: A sparse, warm phrase on piano or soft strings.

shots.title: Sprinklers
shots.sourceExcerpt: Sana moves the cup aside and takes Lea’s hand. Neither looks at the other. They watch the gardener turn on the sprinklers.
shots.description: Cut to a wide shot from behind the bench. Lea and Sana are seen from the back, hands joined between them, with the garden opening up beyond. Neither looks at the other. Both watch the gardener in the middle distance as he turns on the sprinklers and water begins to arc across the garden. The camera slowly drifts back, widening the view. Ending composition: the two small seated figures, hands linked, framed against the spraying sprinklers in the morning light.
shots.atmosphere: Calm, quietly reconciled closeness, with morning light catching the water spray.
shots.music: The gentle phrase resolves softly under the hiss of the sprinklers.
